challenges.name: catalog-pure-functions-quiz
challenges.title: Shared arrays and stable pages
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the catalog: the code that shipped the Newest tab, and two API responses that put tied courses in a different order.

questions.explanation: True. Both useQuery calls share the key ["courses"], so they return the same cached array object, and Array.prototype.sort reorders that array in place and returns it. NewestTab has therefore rewritten the cache entry: the sidebar's slice(0, 5) now takes the five newest courses, not the five best rated. Because React was not told about the change, the sidebar may show the wrong order only after its next re-render, which makes the bug look intermittent. The fix is to sort a copy ([...data].sort(...) or data.toSorted(...)) inside a pure function. The misconception is that data from a hook is a private copy for each component; with a shared cache it is shared state.

questions.question:
The Top rated tab paginates with:

const sorted = [...courses].sort((a, b) => b.rating - a.rating);
const pageItems = sorted.slice((page - 1) * 2, page * 2);   // 2 per page

Two responses of GET /courses, one before and one after a background refetch (same courses, different order):

response 1: c07 (4.8), c03 (4.9), c11 (4.8), c02 (4.6)
response 2: c03 (4.9), c11 (4.8), c02 (4.6), c07 (4.8)

A learner loads page 1 from response 1, the refetch lands, then the learner opens page 2.

Statement: "Because Array.prototype.sort is stable, this code produces the same order from both responses, so page 2 cannot repeat a course from page 1."
questions.explanation: False. A stable sort keeps tied elements in their input order, and the input order is different in the two responses. Response 1 sorts to c03, c07, c11, c02 (c07 came before c11); response 2 sorts to c03, c11, c07, c02. Page 1 from response 1 is c03, c07; page 2 from response 2 is c07, c02: c07 appears twice and c11 is never shown. Stability guarantees consistency for one input, not across inputs. The fix is a total order: end the comparator with a unique key, for example `|| (a.id < b.id ? -1 : 1)`, so ties come out the same way whatever order the API used. The misconception is that "stable" means "deterministic for the same set of items".

challenges.name: catalog-filter-sort-paginate
challenges.title: Filter, sort and paginate the catalog
challenges.description: The CodeDev catalog page sorted the cached course list with .sort() during render, so the "Newest" tab also reordered the "Top rated" sidebar, and tied courses moved between pages after a refetch. Write selectCatalogPage(courses, query) as a pure function. Search: query.search trimmed and case-insensitive, kept when the title contains it; an empty search keeps everything. Filters: category and level must equal the query's values, "all" turns a filter off. Sort: "rating" highest first, "newest" latest publishedAt first (ISO dates, compare as strings), "title" A to Z by title.toLowerCase() compared with < and >; ties are ordered by id A to Z. Paginate: total = matching courses, totalPages = Math.ceil(total / pageSize) but at least 1, the page clamped into 1..totalPages, items = that page's courses. Return { items, page, totalPages, total } and never change the courses array or its courses. The test runner reads { courses, queries } as JSON, runs every query on the same array in order, and prints each page (items as ids) and whether the array is unchanged at the end.
hints: Which array methods return a new array and which change the array you call them on? Where in your function could the original array end up being sorted?

Look at the order of the steps: filter first, then sort, then compute total and totalPages, then clamp the page, and only then slice. For the sort, the comparator needs a second comparison that only runs when the first one says the two courses are equal.

A similar task on another list: ranking leaderboard entries by score (high first), then userId. [...entries].sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score || (a.userId < b.userId ? -1 : a.userId > b.userId ? 1 : 0)). With 7 entries and 3 per page, totalPages is 3; a request for page 5 becomes page 3 and returns the 7th entry alone; with 0 entries it is page 1 of 1 with no items.
